newsitem.title: USA: Clinton signs bill to privatize muni bond insurer.
newsitem.headline: Clinton signs bill to privatize muni bond insurer.

text.p: President Clinton late on Monday signed legislation to expand and privatize Connie Lee, in a move that could set the stage for the company to become a larger player in the municipal bond insurance industry.
Previously, Connie Lee was a so-called "government sponsored enterprise" with a charter that limited it to guaranteeing municipal bonds for colleges and academic hospitals.

The bill signed last night "frees Connie Lee to immediately guarantee bonds in new market sectors such as municipal infastructure and asset-backed obligations," the group said in a press statement on Tuesday.
But Connie Lee must continue to guarantee college and hospital bonds with lower investment grade ratings, under the bill, Connie Lee said.
The new law calls for the U.S. Department of Education, which owns 14 percent of Connie Lee's stock, to divest the holdings within five months.
Proceeds from the divestiture will go to finance public school construction and repairs in the financially strapped District of Columbia, Connie Lee said.

The provision to privatize Connie Lee is part of the omnibus fiscal year 1997 appropriations measure passed by Congress yesterday. It is designed to fund government programs and operations through September 30, 1997.
